body:
# Summary

When publishing to a named index, `uv publish` already resolves the index configuration from `pyproject.toml`, including the configured `publish-url`. However, it does not appear to reuse the username associated with that same index via `UV_INDEX_<NAME>_USERNAME`.

As a result, publishing prompts for a username even though the username for the selected index is already known and is successfully used for package index access.

This behavior is surprising because:

1. `uv publish` is invoked with a specific named index.
2. The index username is already configured.
3. The username is required for successful keyring lookup.
4. The same configuration is already being used for interactions with the index.
5. The same configuration is able to download packages from the private feed

> [!NOTE]  I have redacted index name and urls.

# Environment

- uv 0.13.1
- Windows
- Azure Artifacts
- `artifacts-keyring`
- `UV_KEYRING_PROVIDER=subprocess`
- UV_INDEX_<NAME>_USERNAME=VssSessionToken

# Configuration

`pyproject.toml`

```toml
[[tool.uv.index]]
name = "<NAME>"
explicit = true
url = "https://pkgs.dev.azure.com/maastro/_packaging/<NAME>/pypi/simple/"
publish-url = "https://pkgs.dev.azure.com/**REDACTED**/_packaging/<NAME>/pypi/upload/"
```

Environment variables:

```cmd
UV_INDEX_<NAME>_USERNAME=VssSessionToken
UV_KEYRING_PROVIDER=subprocess
```

# Reproduction

Run:

```bash
uv publish --index <NAME> --keyring-provider subprocess
```

The command prompts for a username:

```text
Enter username ('__token__' if using a token):
```

If `__token__` is entered, publishing fails with:

```text
401 Unauthorized
```

# Observed Behavior

`uv publish` does not appear to automatically use:

```text
UV_INDEX_MAASTRO_PYTHON_FEED_USERNAME=VssSessionToken
```

for the selected index.

Publishing succeeds only when the username is explicitly supplied:

```bash
uv publish \
  --index <NAME> \
  --username VssSessionToken \
  --keyring-provider subprocess
```

# Expected Behavior

When a named index is supplied:

```bash
uv publish --index maastro-python-feed
```

and that index already has a configured username through:

```text
UV_INDEX_MAASTRO_PYTHON_FEED_USERNAME
```

`uv publish` should automatically reuse that username during authentication before prompting the user.

Since `uv publish` already resolves the named index configuration (including `publish-url`), it seems reasonable to expect it to also reuse the username associated with that index.

# Why This Matters

For Azure Artifacts, the username is not arbitrary when using keyring authentication. The username must be:

```text
VssSessionToken
```

Requiring users to provide the username a second time means the configuration associated with the selected index is only partially reused.

It also creates an inconsistency between:

- index access (`UV_INDEX_<NAME>_USERNAME` is used)
- publishing (`--username` or `UV_PUBLISH_USERNAME` appears to be required)

# Suggested Improvement

When `--index <name>` is specified:

1. Resolve the index configuration.
2. Reuse any configured username associated with that index.
3. Fall back to publish-specific credentials or interactive prompts only if no index username is available.

# Workaround

Publishing succeeds when the username is explicitly provided:

```bash
uv publish \
  --index <NAME> \
  --username VssSessionToken \
  --keyring-provider subprocess
```

or by setting:

```cmd
UV_PUBLISH_USERNAME=VssSessionToken
```

# Question

Is the current behavior intentional, or would it make sense for `uv publish --index <name>` to reuse the username already associated with the selected index?
title: `uv publish --index <name>` does not reuse `UV_INDEX_<NAME>_USERNAME` for keyring authentication
